prs.title: Enable agent upgrade reminders by default
prs.author: devjiwonchoi
prs.body:
### Why?

Enable agent upgrade reminders by default and give the experimental Future Defaults policy a clear name.

### How?

Rename `experimental.agenticAutoUpgrade` to `experimental.agentUpgrade` across config, runtime, docs, tests, and evals. Default it to `true`, which normalizes to the `security` policy while preserving explicit policies and `false`. Rename the `future` policy value to `experimental-future`, reuse the development advisory assessment, and preserve CI agent reminders.

Closes NAR-940

prs.title: fix: revalidateTag not reaching custom cache handlers when profiles differ
prs.author: Samiislam851
prs.body:
Fix `updateTags` skipping cache handlers when a request uses multiple cache profiles.

## Why

`getCacheHandlers()` returns a one-time iterator. When tags are grouped by profile, the first group consumes the iterator, so subsequent groups don't reach any handlers.

This is especially noticeable with custom cache handlers, where tags may not be propagated to other instances.

## How

Convert the handlers iterator to an array once and reuse it for each profile group.

## Test

Added an E2E test covering `updateTag()` and `revalidateTag()` with different profiles.

Fixes #99352

prs.title: Prepare image options without mutating configuration
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
## Summary

Image helpers and components sort arrays from their configuration, which fails when that configuration comes from a frozen deployment manifest. Prepare owned image options once and reuse them across rendering and `getImageProps`. This supports immutable Next.js configuration in Vercel adapter deployments.

Modern and legacy Image components share a `useImageConfig` hook that preserves existing configuration selection and SSR `localPatterns` validation. `getImageProps` prepares its fixed options once at module initialization without context.

## Verification

Existing local-pattern, query-string validation, and custom-loader production fixtures pass with Webpack and Turbopack. Development checks cover local patterns, legacy remote-image rejection, and the static-export diagnostic with both bundlers.

prs.title: Finalize the App Router dev indicator on output completion
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
## Summary

Continue removing request-event dependencies from App Router rendering. The request body's `end` event is not a render-completion signal and may already have fired before a custom server invokes Next.

Keep the dev indicator Pending until HTML or Flight output completes, then classify from render-phase dynamic API usage and route configuration, including usage discovered during Client Component SSR. Completion handling stays local and dev-only, without shared lifecycle callbacks or stream helper APIs.

Actions and prefetches do not reclassify the page. HEAD requests preserve the last completed classification because their output is not consumed. Pages Router and Cache Components behavior is unchanged.

## Verification

- Gated browser regressions fail before the change and pass afterward, including a Client Component that calls `unstable_noStore()` after suspending during SSR.
- All 21 dev-indicator tests pass in each combination of Turbopack/Webpack and Cache Components on/off.
- Isolated `pnpm test-start-webpack test/e2e/app-dir/app/standalone.test.ts` passes (2/2).

prs.title: fix(incremental-cache): keep an ISR entry's cache lifetime across instances and restarts
prs.author: orzazade
prs.body:
### What?

An on-demand ISR page (dynamic route with `revalidate`, not prerendered at build) loses its `Cache-Control` header when the process serving it from the cache is not the one that rendered it. That happens with several instances sharing a cache handler, and with a single instance after a restart, including the default file-system cache.

After a restart it is also served `STALE` on every request, because `calculateRevalidate` falls back to its 1-second default.

A running instance can also retain an outdated lifetime after another instance replaces the shared entry with a shorter-lived result.

### Why?

`IncrementalCache.get()` takes an entry's lifetime only from `SharedCacheControls`: an in-memory map that `IncrementalCache.set()` fills in the same process, with the prerender manifest as fallback. An on-demand page of a dynamic route is not in the manifest. So any other process has no lifetime for the entry, sends no header, and treats the entry as stale after one second.

### How?

- `CacheHandlerValue` gets an optional `cacheControl`. Handlers already receive it as `ctx.cacheControl` in `set()`; now they can return it from `get()`.
- In `IncrementalCache.get()`, the lifetime returned with the entry takes precedence over the in-memory map and is remembered for the route, so both the response header and revalidation use the entry's current lifetime.
- The default `FileSystemCache` stores `cacheControl` in the `.meta` file of App Router pages and routes, and returns
…(truncated)

prs.title: turbo-persistence: space-amplification driven compaction with adaptive hash shards
prs.author: lukesandberg
prs.body:
## Summary

Turbo-tasks GC can only shrink the persistent cache if compaction merges each tombstone with the data it deletes. Canary's compaction algorithm leaves many tombstones behind so with GC enabled the cache is only 5% smaller than without it. This PR replaces compaction with a space-amplification policy on hash shards, modeled on RocksDB universal compaction and Cassandra UCS. With GC enabled, the cache stays ~flat.

### Cache size over 31 consecutive vercel-site builds

Same canary base and the same commits in every arm. The size is measured after each build, including its compaction on shutdown.

| build | canary, GC off | canary, GC on | this PR, GC off | this PR, GC on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.59 GB | 2.60 GB | 2.63 GB | 2.64 GB |
| 10 | 3.15 GB | 3.12 GB | 3.24 GB | 3.07 GB |
| 20 | 3.42 GB | 2.92 GB | 3.20 GB | 3.06 GB |
| 22 | 4.57 GB | 3.87 GB | 3.55 GB | 3.18 GB |
| 31 | **4.19 GB** | **3.96 GB** | **3.75 GB** | **3.00 GB** |
| growth, build 1 → 31 | +1.60 GB | +1.36 GB | +1.12 GB | **+0.36 GB** |

- **GC saves 5% with canary's compaction and 20% with this one** (final size, GC on vs. off). A full compaction of the final cache puts the live data at about 2.8 GB, so this PR with GC is within about 8% of it.
- **Build 22 rewrites a lot of task data.** Canary grows by about 1 GB at that build in both modes and never recovers the space. This PR absorbs it and merges the superseded versions away within a few builds.

prs.title: fix: propagate repeated tag revalidation from after()
prs.author: uaoa
prs.body:
## What

Propagate a repeated revalidation of the same tag and profile from an `after()` callback when its timestamp advances during the request. Add an E2E test that refills the tagged cache entry between the two calls.

## Why

`revalidateTag()` updates `revalidatedAt` on an existing pending item in place. `withExecuteRevalidates()` currently saves a shallow copy of that item, and `diffRevalidationState()` only compares tag and profile. The second call is therefore dropped, leaving an entry refilled between calls stale. The reproduction uses the built-in cache handler and returns `{ source: 2, cached: 1 }` where `{ source: 2, cached: 2 }` is expected.

## How

Snapshot the pending tag items and compare `revalidatedAt` for matching tag/profile pairs. The regression test holds the `after()` callback until a request has refilled the cache, then checks that the final read is fresh.

The production reproduction passed with the equivalent runtime change on `next@16.4.0-canary.53`. `git diff --check` passed. The full monorepo E2E suite has not been run locally.

Fixes #99498

prs.title: Set tracer library version
prs.author: lukahartwig
prs.body:
### What?

Sets the correct Next.js library version for Otel traces.

### Why?

The tracer instance was configured with a hard coded "0.0.1" library version. This is confusing since it makes it look like trace spans were produced by `next@0.0.1`. Instead I'm setting the library version to the current Next.js version.

### How?

I'm using the `__NEXT_VERSION` env var, which gets replaced by the package.json version during build.

prs.title: Pass App Page HMR state through a dev render context
prs.author: gnoff
prs.body:
## Summary

Continue decoupling App Router rendering from incoming request objects by capturing HMR state at the handler boundary and passing it through DevRenderContext.

The context contains the HMR refresh hash and shared server-component HMR cache, and is constructed only under `next dev`. Production omits this state, and prerendering does not consume it. Rendering no longer reads the hash from request metadata. Existing upstream metadata transport and cache invalidation behavior are preserved; status and debugging callbacks are left for separate migrations.

## Verification

- `pnpm test-dev-turbo test/development/app-dir/use-cache-dev/use-cache-dev.test.ts` (7 tests)
- `pnpm test-dev-webpack test/development/app-dir/use-cache-dev/use-cache-dev.test.ts` (7 tests)

prs.author: devjiwonchoi
prs.body:
### Why?

Running a codemod through `npx` can select npm even when the app declares Yarn, pnpm, or Bun, causing dependency installation to fail.

### How?

Read `package.json#packageManager` before `npm_config_user_agent`. Keep the existing user-agent, lockfile, and npm fallbacks unchanged.

Add shared checks for installation and recovery after an interrupted upgrade.

prs.title: Enable Turbopack export name mangling by default for builds
prs.author: sokra
prs.body:
### What?

`experimental.turbopackMangleExportNames` is now on by default for production builds (`next build`) in both stable and canary releases. It stays off by default in development (`next dev`), and an explicit `true`/`false` in `next.config` still wins in either mode.

### Why?

Mangling export names shortens the keys modules use to link to each other, which reduces bundle size. Until now it was only on by default in canary builds, because stable releases pinned it to `false`.

### How?

Turbopack already chooses the default from the build mode in `NextConfig::turbopack_mangle_export_names`: if the option is unset, it's enabled everywhere except development, and an explicit value overrides that. The only thing keeping it off on stable was the JS default config, which forced `false` when `isStableBuild()` was true. That pin is removed, so the default stays unset on every release channel and the Rust side decides from the build mode. There's no change to Rust or to the mangling itself.

The JSDoc on the config type and the Turbopack config docs table now say the default is `false` in dev and `true` for builds.

### Verification

- Prettier and ESLint pass on the changed files.
- `pnpm --filter=next types`: only 3 `TS2307` errors, all for missing generated `dist` modules (`@next/font`, `@vercel/og`) in an unbootstrapped checkout. The same errors show up without this change, and none are in `config-shared.ts`.
- Not run: a bootstrapped integration build. CI covers the build

prs.title: Remove suspend during operations
prs.author: jimmyhmiller
prs.body:
## What

Remove the ability to suspend in flight operations to allow for snapshotting and GC

## Why

Exstensive testing with GC has revealed a number of bugs latent in this system

* transient task ids are getting serialized as part of operations, this confuses our new stricter task access semantics in fresh sessions
* child execution contexts don't properly participate, they both need to suspend when requested to avoid exceeding retries since the task they are waiting for has already suspended, and cannot suspend because that could deadlock the scope_bounded call

Instead we just don't suspend.  This simplifies a lot, should be a small perf win (purely from not touching the atomics as often)

The major risk is that waiting for everything to settle adds latency.  To mitigate that:

* idle snapshots don't wait for operations to settle, they just bail out instead
* other snapshots do wait but log warnings if it takes more than 10s, this should never happen but if it does we will have a smoking gun

prs.title: turbo-persistence: 32 bit fingerprints for the used keys AMQFs
prs.author: lukesandberg
prs.body:
## What

decrease the size of the used key amqfs to 32 bits

## Why
Save disk space, compaction will also be a bit faster due to smaller filters which are cheaper to query and merge.

All filters keep the same fingerprint size, so their union still uses qfilter's sorted merge.

## Verification

- Re-encoding the used keys AMQFs of the final cache of a 31-build vercel-site run (GC on): **61.8 MB → 17.8 MB** (7.96 → 2.29 bytes per key), about 1.5% of the 2.96 GB cache. GC off: 58.9 → 16.9 MB.
- `cargo test -p turbo-persistence` and `cargo test -p turbo-tasks-backend --tests` pass.

prs.title: Measure AI upgrade nudges, handoffs, and completion
prs.author: devjiwonchoi
prs.body:
> [!TIP]
> Recommended to review commit by commit with "Hide whitespace" enabled.

### Why?

Measure how often humans and agents receive upgrade nudges, start AI upgrades, and finish them.

### How?

Record the configured policy, shown nudges, human decisions, AI upgrade runs, CLI results, and agent results through existing Next.js telemetry. Existing telemetry opt-out settings apply.

`next upgrade --ai` prepares an upgrade prompt and hands it to an agent. The prompt asks the agent to run `next internal report-ai-upgrade <run-id> success|failure` after completing the upgrade and verification. The run ID links this report to the original upgrade run.

Completion reporting depends on the agent following that instruction. A missing report means unknown, not failure. The prompt does not instruct the agent to hide reporting or require it to mention the telemetry submission to the user. The reporting command suppresses the normal telemetry notice.

Closes NAR-938
